purpose: Close point 1 of #4890: nothing on the deploy path checked that the API's own database principal cannot bypass row level security. The DATABASE_URL parser reads the role name and asserts only that it is non-empty, so an admin role would deploy cleanly and every RLS policy in this repository would be inert with no gate noticing. The gate runs before apply_tai_migrations, so a violation stops the deploy with the database untouched.
requiredInvariants: Point 1 of #4890 only. Nothing is migrated to a confined role, no production value is read or written, and no claim is made about what the VPS env file currently contains - that remains the owner action the issue names. This pass makes the open question a fail-closed invariant; it does not answer it.
The gate is a check. It changes no deploy behaviour on a conforming deployment, and it runs before apply_tai_migrations so a refusal costs nothing and leaves the database untouched.

rolsuper and rolbypassrls alone are NOT the check, because measurement showed they are not sufficient. Three further shapes read f/f and still bypass: a role GRANTed a BYPASSRLS role, a role GRANTed a superuser role, and the owner of an RLS table that lacks FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.

Membership is tested with pg_has_role 'MEMBER', not 'USAGE'. Measured on a NOINHERIT member: USAGE reads false, MEMBER reads true, and the role reads every row after SET ROLE. A USAGE-based gate would clear a principal that can take the bypass whenever it likes.
The ownership clause keys on the missing FORCE rather than on ownership, proven both ways: the owner is flagged without FORCE and cleared with it, and its actual row count moves with the verdict.

The proof does not restate the gate. It extracts the SQL out of scripts/tai-reg-ru-deploy.sh and runs that exact text, so it cannot drift from what deploys - a second copy kept correct by attention is how the #4683 docstring went stale.
No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation. No migration, no schema change, no new dependency, no lockfile change. New mandatory cost: 0 RUB.
acceptance: Six role shapes plus the FORCE case, each asserted twice: what the gate reports, and how many rows the role can actually read through a USING (false) policy. A gate whose verdict disagreed with the row count would be reporting something other than a bypass.

Measured correspondence, no false positive and no false negative: confined role 0 rows and no finding; direct BYPASSRLS 2 rows; owner without FORCE 2 rows; owner with FORCE 0 rows and no finding; both membership shapes 0 rows as themselves and 2 after the SET ROLE hop they are entitled to take.

Six mutations, all caught: MEMBER to USAGE; ownership clause removed; ownership clause re-narrowed to schema public; direct BYPASSRLS clause removed; SUPERUSER clause removed; DB_APP_USER export removed.

Two of those six escaped the first version of the proof and the proof was strengthened rather than the result reported. MEMBER-to-USAGE escaped because both membership probes used INHERIT, where USAGE and MEMBER agree - a NOINHERIT probe was added, which is the only shape that separates them. Removing the SUPERUSER clause escaped because no probe role was a real superuser and the probe cannot create one unless it already is one - the clause is now asserted against a superuser the cluster already has, which on the deploy path is exactly the compose POSTGRES_USER this issue is about.

The proof also found a real limitation in the first gate: it scoped ownership to schema public, so an RLS table owned by the API principal in any other schema was invisible to it. Widened to every non-system schema and the finding is schema-qualified.
The gate's exit code 27 was free; returns in this script stop at 26.
TAI REG.RU deployment contract PASS with 28 negative fixtures; shell syntax check clean; api-test.yml parses.
